newsitem.title: UK: Husband, sons found guilty of murdering teacher.
newsitem.headline: Husband, sons found guilty of murdering teacher.

text.p: The husband and two teenage sons of a 48-year-old teacher were found guilty of her murder by a British court on Tuesday, despite evidence they suffered years of emotional and physical abuse at her hands.
David Howells, 48, and his sons, Glenn, 17, and John, 16, were found guilty of murdering Eve Howells at their home in Huddersfield, northern England.
The judge at the court in Leeds, Sir john Alliott, said the three would automatically be given life sentences.
But he took the unusual step of delaying sentencing until he could talk to their lawyers.
"I feel even now that although I entirely endorse the verdicts of the jury I don't know the whole truth," he said.
All three had pleaded not guilty and their lawyer said on Tuesday they were considering an appeal.
Glenn, 15 at the time of the killing, admitted hitting his mother 10 times with a hammer. But he told the court during the trial he had suffered years of abuse from his mother.
The court was told Eve Howells, who was having an affair with her husband's best friend and colleague, Russell Hirst, screamed, shouted and spat at her children.
The boys were rarely allowed out to play and were dragged by the hair if they failed to come immediately they were called.
When they were toddlers, she would take their cuddly toys and threaten to burn them with a lighter.

Eve Howells, a teacher whose strict discipline in the classroom provoked complaints from pupils and parents, was believed to have had an eating disorder, weighing only 84 lbs (38 kg) when she died and keeping the freezer padlocked.
Glenn repeatedly called a helpline for abused children, only to put it down when it was answered, and even considered suicide, psychologists told the court.
But, in a claim which sparked bitter recriminations between David and his sons, John told the court the murder had been planned together with Glenn and his father.
David Howells, an alcoholic, dismissed the claim as lies, saying he had been playing darts at a club when his wife died.
He was trapped by secret police tapes of him telling his sons to admit nothing and promising to use the 155,000 pounds ($253,300) left by his wife to take them abroad and buy them jet skis.
In a final twist, the conviction of the three means that his wife's lover, Russell Hirst, who was mentioned in her will, will now inherit all her money. ($1=.6120 Pound)
